constraints.text: GracefulStop / GracefulStopForget (settled? = ztrue): the held outbox of every session, and mail of a read that settled, is filed back to the relay before the daemon closes; the relay's mail is untouched
constraints.verifiedBy: read from branch pl-consuming-read-cancel (head 9aa72c8). The first: a consuming relay whose fetch_user_inbox consumes the mail and stalls 0.3 s; harness.daemon.stop() is called while a read is mid-fetch; a new BiffDaemon (request_timeout 0.5) is queried by a cli client for the session and returns the mail ('do not lose me'): the settle step waits for the read and the hand-over files it. The second is parametrised over consuming and non-consuming relays: a seat holds an unconfirmed batch (request_held 'read'), the daemon is stopped and revived, and a reattached read returns it ('in flight'). Both restart a daemon that has forgotten its harness records, so they exercise GracefulStopForget, not the durable GracefulStop; the filing is the same step

limitsWithoutTest.text: GracefulStop with settled? = zfalse (the settle step times out with a read in flight): the mail that read consumed and had not handed to the outbox is lost; unread relay mail is safe
limitsWithoutTest.reason: Handback.close_relays runs Uncancellable.settle(core.request_timeout), which only logs a warning when a task outlives the timeout. Neither PR 675 test makes a read outlast the bound (the first stalls 0.3 s against a 0.5 s timeout). The model states the loss as lostN > 0 with lastStop = sTimedOut; the loss is the price of a bounded stop, not a defect, but nothing in tests/ shows it happens as modelled. A test needs a fetch that stalls beyond request_timeout and asserts the warning and the lost batch

limitsWithoutTest.text: ProcessLoss: the crash loses the outbox and any read in flight (PL-1753), and the forgotten harness records (PL-1771)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: PR 675 replaces the only test that asserted a loss, because a graceful stop no longer loses the outbox. A crash cannot be tested in-process; the loss is a documented limit, kept in the model as ProcessLoss and ProcessLossForget

limitsWithoutTest.text: GracefulStopForget, ProcessLossForget, RowAgesOut, TtyAgesOut: the code keeps harness records in memory, so a restart forgets them; the row and (on NATS) the name age out by the relay's lifetime, the local relay's name reservation has no lifetime, and the restarted session's own relay inbox is stranded (strandedN; the user's mailbox is untouched)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: a divergence from the durable-record model, reported as a finding (PL-1771 tracks the code fix): a name held up to the row lifetime, or for good on the local relay, and unread session-inbox mail never drained to the user mailbox. No test asserts the forgotten record or the stranding
